1: ---
     2: - name: Gather service facts

    13:     - "ansible_service_mgr == 'systemd'"
    14:     - "'jenkins.service' in ansible_facts.services"
    15:     - "ansible_facts.services['jenkins.service']['state'] != 'stopped'"
    16: 
    17: - name: Set jenkins_service_running for SysV init hosts
    18:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    19:     jenkins_service_running: true
    20:   when:
    21:     - "ansible_service_mgr == 'sysvinit'"
    22:     - "'jenkins' in ansible_facts.services"
    23:     - "ansible_facts.services['jenkins']['state'] != 'stopped'"
    24: 
    25: - name: Stop Jenkins service
    26:   when: jenkins_service_running | bool
    27:   block:
    28:     - name: Slurp Jenkins service PID
    29:       ansible.builtin.slurp:
    30:         path: "{{ jenkins_pid_file }}"
    31:       register: jenkins_pid
    32: 
    33:     - name: Ensure Jenkins service is stopped
    34:       become: true
    35:       ansible.builtin.service:
    36:         enabled: false
    37:         name: "jenkins"
    38:         state: stopped
    39:         # This normally isn't required, but we also test this role in Docker containers
    40:         # that resemble standalone hosts with SSH. Since OpenSSH has libsystemd as a
    41:         # dependency, it will fool the service module into selecting systemd as the
    42:         # service backend.
    43:         use: "{{ ansible_service_mgr }}"
    44:       # This is required or else molecule's idempotency test will fail. See:
    45:       # https://github.com/ansible-community/molecule/issues/2765
    46:       changed_when: false
    47:       when: not ansible_check_mode
    48: 
    49:     # Just to be safe, wait until Jenkins finally stops. Stopping services can be
    50:     # asynchronous and so the process itself may continue to run for a bit to ensure a
    51:     # clean shut-down. If subsequent tasks must do something with files in the Jenkins
    52:     # home folder, this may cause problems.
    53:     - name: Wait for Jenkins service to stop
    54:       ansible.builtin.command:
    55:         cmd: "ps -p {{ jenkins_pid['content'] | b64decode }}"
    56:       register: jenkins_service_running
    57:       ignore_errors: true
    58:       until: jenkins_service_running is failed
    59:       retries: 60
    60:       delay: 1
    61:       # This is required or else molecule's idempotency test will fail. See:
    62:       # https://github.com/ansible-community/molecule/issues/2765
    63:       changed_when: false
    64:       when: not ansible_check_mode
    65: 
    66:     # Again, a paranoid measure aimed at preventing potential errors when immediately
    67:     # accessing files in the Jenkins home folder.
    68:     - name: Sync filesystems
    69:       ansible.builtin.command:
    70:         cmd: "sync"

    22:       register: running_containers_raw
    23:       changed_when: false

    26:     - name: Build aqa_containers data structure
    27:       vars:
    28:         # Each line: "<name>|||<image>|||<ports>"

    30:         parsed: >-
    31:           {{
    32:             running_containers_raw.stdout_lines

    35:           }}

    51:                             else item[0].split('.')[-1],
    52:               'isArm32':    item[0].upper().endswith('.ARM32'),
    53:               'dockerfile': dockerfile_path if dockerfile_exists else None
    54:             }]
    55:           }}

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # This playbook shrinks Ceph OSDs that have been created with ceph-volume.
     3: # It can remove any number of OSD(s) from the cluster and ALL THEIR DATA
     4: #
     5: # Use it like this:
     6: # ansible-playbook shrink-osd.yml -e osd_to_kill=0,2,6
     7: #     Prompts for confirmation to shrink, defaults to no and
     8: #     doesn't shrink the cluster. yes shrinks the cluster.
     9: #
    10: # ansible-playbook -e ireallymeanit=yes|no shrink-osd.yml
    11: #     Overrides the prompt using -e option. Can be used in
    12: #     automation scripts to avoid interactive prompt.
    13: 
    14: - name: Gather facts and check the init system
    15:   hosts:
    16:     - mons
    17:     - osds
    18: 
    19:   become: true
    20:   tasks:
    21:     - name: Gather facts on all Ceph hosts for following reference
    22:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    23:         msg: "gather facts on all Ceph hosts for following reference"
    24: 
    25: - name: Confirm whether user really meant to remove osd(s) from the cluster
    26:   hosts: mons[0]
    27:   become: true
    28:   vars_prompt:
    29:     - name: ireallymeanit  # noqa: name[casing]
    30:       prompt: Are you sure you want to shrink the cluster?
    31:       default: 'no'
    32:       private: false
    33:   vars:
    34:     mon_group_name: mons
    35:     osd_group_name: osds
    36: 
    37:   pre_tasks:
    38:     - name: Exit playbook, if user did not mean to shrink cluster
    39:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    40:         msg: "Exiting shrink-osd playbook, no osd(s) was/were removed..
    41:            To shrink the cluster, either say 'yes' on the prompt or
    42:            or use `-e ireallymeanit=yes` on the command line when
    43:            invoking the playbook"
    44:       when: ireallymeanit != 'yes'
    45: 
    46:     - name: Exit playbook, if no osd(s) was/were given
    47:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    48:         msg: "osd_to_kill must be declared
    49:           Exiting shrink-osd playbook, no OSD(s) was/were removed.
    50:            On the command line when invoking the playbook, you can use
    51:            -e osd_to_kill=0,1,2,3 argument."
    52:       when: osd_to_kill is not defined
    53: 
    54:     - name: Check the osd ids passed have the correct format
    55:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    56:         msg: "The id {{ item }} has wrong format, please pass the number only"
    57:       with_items: "{{ osd_to_kill.split(',') }}"
    58:       when: not item is regex("^\d+$")
    59: 
    60:   tasks:
    61:     - name: Import ceph-defaults role

    63:         name: ceph-defaults
    64: 
    65:     - name: Import ceph-facts role
    66:       ansible.builtin.import_role:
    67:         name: ceph-facts
    68:         tasks_from: container_binary
    69: 
    70:   post_tasks:
    71:     - name: Set_fact container_exec_cmd build docker exec command (containerized)
    72:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    73:         container_exec_cmd: "{{ container_binary }} exec ceph-mon-{{ ansible_facts['hostname'] }}"
    74:       when: containerized_deployment | bool
    75: 
    76:     - name: Exit playbook, if can not connect to the cluster
    77:       ansible.builtin.command: "{{ container_exec_cmd }} timeout 5 ceph --cluster {{ cluster }} health"
    78:       register: ceph_health
    79:       changed_when: false

    81:       retries: 5
    82:       delay: 2
    83: 
    84:     - name: Find the host(s) where the osd(s) is/are running on

    86:       changed_when: false

    88:       register: find_osd_hosts
    89: 
    90:     - name: Set_fact osd_hosts
    91:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    92:         osd_hosts: "{{ osd_hosts | default([]) + [[(item.stdout | from_json).crush_location.host, (item.stdout | from_json).osd_fsid, item.item]] }}"
    93:       with_items: "{{ find_osd_hosts.results }}"
    94: 
    95:     - name: Set_fact _osd_hosts
    96:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    97:         _osd_hosts: "{{ _osd_hosts | default([]) + [ [ item.0, item.2, item.3 ] ] }}"
    98:       with_nested:
    99:         - "{{ groups.get(osd_group_name) }}"

   102:

   143:       changed_when: false

   161:           delegate_to: "{{ item.0 }}"
   162:           when: item.2 not in _lvm_list.keys()
   163:           loop: "{{ _osd_hosts }}"
   164: 
   165:         - name: Activate OSD
   166:           ansible.builtin.command: |

   168:             -v /dev:/dev -v /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
   169:             -v /var/lib/ceph/tmp/:/var/lib/ceph/osd:z,rshared
   170:             -v /etc/ceph:/etc/ceph:z -v /var/run/ceph:/var/run/ceph:z
   171:             -v /var/run/udev/:/var/run/udev/ -v /var/log/ceph:/var/log/ceph:z
   172:             -e OSD_BLUESTORE=1 -e OSD_FILESTORE=0 -e OSD_DMCRYPT=0 -e CLUSTER=ceph -e DEBUG=verbose

   183:

   187:             -v /dev:/dev -v /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro

   189:             -v /etc/ceph:/etc/ceph:z -v /var/run/ceph:/var/run/ceph:z

   194:             -e OSD_ID={{ item.2 }}

name: roles/vikunja/tasks/operator_access_one.yml
review_question: Does this playbook have harmful dependency coupling?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Share every project owned by ONE automation account with the operator.
     3: # Included per item from operator_access.yml with loop_var: vikunja_share_owner
     4: # (a username string; its password comes from vikunja_share_owner_password_map).
     5: #
     6: # Acting as the owner via a password JWT — not via a minted MCP API token — is
     7: # deliberate. The MCP tokens are bounded to the task-management route groups
     8: # (vikunja_mcp_token_scopes), and project sharing is a permission-management
     9: # route outside that scope. The JWT carries exactly the owner's own rights and
    10: # nothing broader, and only a project's owner/admin may share it.
    11: 
    12: - name: "Log in to Vikunja as {{ vikunja_share_owner }}"
    13:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    14:     url: "http://localhost:{{ vikunja_port }}/api/v1/login"
    15:     method: POST
    16:     body_format: json
    17:     body:
    18:       username: "{{ vikunja_share_owner }}"
    19:       password: "{{ vikunja_share_owner_password_map[vikunja_share_owner] }}"
    20:     status_code: [200]
    21:     timeout: "{{ vikunja_api_timeout }}"
    22:   register: vikunja_share_login
    23:   no_log: true
    24: 
    25: # Page 1 also carries the pagination headers, so the remaining page count is
    26: # read from the response rather than assumed. Silently taking only page 1 would
    27: # leave the operator without whichever boards happened to sort onto later pages.
    28: - name: "List the first page of projects visible to {{ vikunja_share_owner }}"
    29:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    30:     url: "http://localhost:{{ vikunja_port }}/api/v1/projects?page=1"
    31:     method: GET
    32:     headers:
    33:       Authorization: "Bearer {{ vikunja_share_login.json.token }}"
    34:     status_code: [200]
    35:     timeout: "{{ vikunja_api_timeout }}"
    36:   register: vikunja_share_projects_p1
    37:   changed_when: false
    38: 
    39: - name: "List the remaining pages of projects visible to {{ vikunja_share_owner }}"
    40:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    41:     url: "http://localhost:{{ vikunja_port }}/api/v1/projects?page={{ item }}"
    42:     method: GET
    43:     headers:
    44:       Authorization: "Bearer {{ vikunja_share_login.json.token }}"
    45:     status_code: [200]
    46:     timeout: "{{ vikunja_api_timeout }}"
    47:   loop: >-
    48:     {{ range(2, (vikunja_share_projects_p1.x_pagination_total_pages
    49:                  | default(1, true) | int) + 1) | list }}
    50:   register: vikunja_share_projects_rest
    51:   changed_when: false
    52: 
    53: # Only projects this account OWNS are in scope. Anything merely shared with it
    54: # belongs to another owner and is covered by that owner's own pass — re-sharing
    55: # it from here would fail anyway, since sharing needs owner/admin rights.
    56: # models.Project exposes the owner as a nested user object (json:"owner").
    57: - name: "Select the projects owned by {{ vikunja_share_owner }}"
    58:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    59:     vikunja_owned_projects: >-
    60:       {{ ((vikunja_share_projects_p1.json | default([], true))
    61:           + (vikunja_share_projects_rest.results | default([], true)
    62:              | map(attribute='json') | select('iterable') | list | flatten))
    63:          | selectattr('owner', 'defined')
    64:          | selectattr('owner.username', 'equalto', vikunja_share_owner)
    65:          | list }}
    66: 
    67: - name: "Reconcile the operator's share on each project owned by {{ vikunja_share_owner }}"
    68:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: operator_access_project.yml
    69:   loop: "{{ vikunja_owned_projects }}"
    70:   loop_control:
    71:     loop_var: vikunja_share_project
    72:     label: "{{ vikunja_share_project.id }}:{{ vikunja_share_project.title | default('') }}"

name: playbooks/site/05-media-and-gate.yml
review_question: Does this playbook have harmful dependency coupling?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # =============================================================================
     3: # The media stack lives in its own repository and is pinned here as a git
     4: # submodule. It runs as its own `ansible-playbook` process, not an
     5: # `import_playbook`: Ansible resolves `group_vars/` against the inventory
     6: # directory and the CLI-invoked playbook only, so importing that repo's
     7: # site.yml would silently drop every one of its group_vars and converge the
     8: # media guests on bare role defaults. A separate process keeps its inventory,
     9: # ansible.cfg and group_vars intact.
    10: #
    11: # This play is what makes the split invisible to anything that drives a full
    12: # converge: `site.yml` remains the single entry point, and the media stack is
    13: # reached automatically with no extra step to remember. Keep it that way — if
    14: # this play is ever removed, the media guests silently stop being converged
    15: # and nothing reports it.
    16: #
    17: # The pin is an immutable SHA recorded by the submodule, the same discipline
    18: # as the collection pins in requirements.yml: a moving ref would let an
    19: # unreviewed change in the other repo reach a converge here without a PR.
    20: # =============================================================================
    21: 
    22: - name: Converge the media stack from its own repository
    23:   hosts: localhost
    24:   connection: local
    25:   gather_facts: false
    26:   tags:
    27:     - media
    28:     - servarr
    29:   vars:
    30:     _servarr_dir: "{{ playbook_dir }}/../../servarr"
    31:     # group_vars/all.yml sets `ansible_become: true` for every host, and a
    32:     # connection variable beats the `become:` play keyword — so this has to be
    33:     # the variable, the same way load_tofu.yml does it. This play only shells
    34:     # out on the control node; the chained run escalates on the guests itself.
    35:     ansible_become: false
    36:   tasks:
    37:     - name: Converge the media stack (isolated — failure does not abort downstream plays)
    38:       when: site_converge_servarr | default(true) | bool
    39:       block:
    40:         # scripts/run-ansible.sh checks the submodule out at its pinned SHA
    41:         # before invoking ansible, so a bare clone needs no preparatory step.
    42:         # Fail here with the reason rather than letting `chdir` report a bare
    43:         # "directory does not exist" from an empty submodule dir.
    44:         - name: Confirm the pinned media-stack submodule is checked out
    45:           ansible.builtin.stat:
    46:             path: "{{ _servarr_dir }}/playbooks/site.yml"
    47:           register: _servarr_stat
    48:           failed_when: not _servarr_stat.stat.exists
    49:           changed_when: false
    50: 
    51:         - name: Run the media stack's own site.yml
    52:           ansible.builtin.command:
    53:             cmd: >-
    54:               scripts/fetch-openbao-secrets.sh media --
    55:               scripts/run-ansible.sh playbooks/site.yml
    56:               {{ '--check' if ansible_check_mode else '' }}
    57:             chdir: "{{ _servarr_dir }}"
    58:           register: _servarr_converge
    59:           changed_when: true
    60:           # This play is the only caller, and it already reports the outcome.
    61:           # `--check` is passed through above rather than skipped, so a dry run
    62:           # of site.yml stays a dry run all the way down.
    63:           check_mode: false
    64: 
    65:         # Without this the chained run is a black box: its per-host recap only
    66:         # exists inside the child process's stdout.
    67:         - name: Report the media stack's recap
    68:           ansible.builtin.debug:
    69:             msg: "{{ _servarr_converge.stdout_lines[-20:] }}"
    70: 
    71:       rescue:
    72:         - name: Surface the media-stack converge output before recording the failure
    73:           ansible.builtin.debug:
    74:             msg: "{{ (_servarr_converge | default({})).stdout_lines | default(['no output captured']) }}"
    75: 
    76:         - name: Record isolated failure and continue
    77:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: ../tasks/record_isolated_failure.yml
    78:           vars:
    79:             _isolated_play_name: servarr
    80: 
    81: - name: Fail the run if any isolated play recorded a failure
    82:   hosts: localhost
    83:   gather_facts: false
    84:   tags:
    85:     - always
    86:   tasks:
    87:     # Failures are recorded host-locally (see tasks/record_isolated_failure.yml
    88:     # — a shared delegated fact would drop entries when hosts fail
    89:     # concurrently), so aggregate across every host's hostvars here.
    90:     - name: Surface isolated play failures
    91:       vars:
    92:         _all_isolated_failures: >-
    93:           {{ groups['all'] | union(['localhost'])
    94:              | map('extract', hostvars, 'site_isolated_failures')
    95:              | select('defined') | flatten }}
    96:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    97:         msg: >-
    98:           {{ _all_isolated_failures | length }} isolated play failure(s) —
    99:           the rest of site.yml still ran: {{ _all_isolated_failures | join('; ') }}
   100:       when: _all_isolated_failures | length > 0

name: playbooks/rpi_netboot/enroll.yml
review_question: Does this playbook have harmful dependency coupling?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Enroll a Pi into netboot management: converge the EEPROM bootloader
     3: # config (BOOT_ORDER, TFTP prefix mode, UART) and capture the identity
     4: # facts the operator must record in inventory (serial, MAC).
     5: #
     6: # This is the one imperative bring-up step Pi netboot cannot avoid — a
     7: # factory Pi must boot once from SD/USB before its EEPROM can be set
     8: # (the analog of persist_uboot_env on SPI boards). The Pi must be
     9: # SSH-reachable when this runs.
    10: #
    11: # The EEPROM TFTP_PREFIX key is derived from the SAME
    12: # rpi_tftp_prefix_mode var the router-side playbooks key their /ip tftp
    13: # rows on, so firmware and router can never disagree about the prefix.
    14: #
    15: # Usage:
    16: #   ansible-playbook playbooks/rpi_netboot/enroll.yml \
    17: #     -i igou-inventory/inventory.yaml -e target_hosts=upsmonitor.igou.systems
    18: - name: Enroll Pi into netboot management (EEPROM + identity capture)
    19:   hosts: "{{ target_hosts | default('rpis') }}"
    20:   gather_facts: false
    21:   become: true
    22:   tasks:
    23:     - name: Resolve effective rpi config
    24:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/_resolve_rpi_config.yml
    25: 
    26:     - name: Refuse to enroll unmanaged hosts
    27:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    28:         that:
    29:           - rpi_netboot_managed
    30:         fail_msg: >-
    31:           {{ inventory_hostname }} has rpi_boot_mode=local — enrolling it
    32:           would flip its BOOT_ORDER to net-first. Set rpi_boot_mode to
    33:           net or sd in inventory first if that is really intended.
    34: 
    35:     - name: Assert the fleet EEPROM golden config is defined
    36:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    37:         that:
    38:           - rpi_eeprom_config is defined
    39:           - rpi_eeprom_config.BOOT_ORDER is defined
    40:         fail_msg: >-
    41:           rpi_eeprom_config (the fleet golden EEPROM settings, at least
    42:           BOOT_ORDER) is unset. It belongs in the rpis group_vars — see
    43:           playbooks/rpi_netboot/README.md.
    44: 
    45:     # Merge order: fleet golden < prefix-mode keys < per-host extras.
    46:     # Empty-string values are dropped from the MANAGED set — the key is
    47:     # left unmanaged (an existing EEPROM value is NOT removed). The
    48:     # inventory uses '' for TFTP_IP when the router is the TFTP server
    49:     # via next-server; a Pi that already carries a stale TFTP_IP must
    50:     # have it cleared manually (rpi-eeprom-config --edit).
    51:     - name: Compose effective EEPROM settings
    52:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    53:         _rpi_enroll_settings: >-
    54:           {{ rpi_eeprom_config
    55:              | combine(rpi_eeprom_prefix_settings)
    56:              | combine(rpi_eeprom_extra_settings | default({}))
    57:              | dict2items
    58:              | rejectattr('value', 'equalto', '')
    59:              | items2dict }}
    60: 
    61:     # Enroll reboots to flash BEFORE any netboot assets are staged — a
    62:     # net-only BOOT_ORDER (e.g. 0x2) would strand the Pi with nothing
    63:     # to boot. Require an SD (1) or USB (4) fallback digit.
    64:     - name: Assert BOOT_ORDER keeps a local fallback
    65:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    66:         that:
    67:           - >-
    68:             (_rpi_enroll_settings.BOOT_ORDER | string) is search('[14]')
    69:             or not (rpi_eeprom_reboot | default(true) | bool)
    70:             or (rpi_enroll_allow_no_local_fallback | default(false) | bool)
    71:         fail_msg: >-
    72:           BOOT_ORDER={{ _rpi_enroll_settings.BOOT_ORDER }} contains no SD
    73:           (1) or USB (4) fallback digit, and enrollment flashes it via
    74:           reboot before stage_netboot_assets has run — the Pi would have
    75:           nothing to boot. Fix rpi_eeprom_config.BOOT_ORDER (e.g. 0xf12),
    76:           or set rpi_enroll_allow_no_local_fallback=true if you really
    77:           mean it.
    78: 
    79:     - name: Converge EEPROM bootloader config
    80:       ansible.builtin.include_role:
    81:         name: rpi_eeprom
    82:       vars:
    83:         rpi_eeprom_settings: "{{ _rpi_enroll_settings }}"
    84: 
    85:     - name: Flag inventory drift against captured identity
    86:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    87:         msg: >-
    88:           WARNING: inventory drift on {{ inventory_hostname }} —
    89:           rpi_serial='{{ rpi_serial | default('') }}' vs captured
    90:           '{{ rpi_eeprom_facts.serial8 }}'; rpi_board_mac='{{ rpi_board_mac }}'
    91:           vs captured '{{ rpi_eeprom_facts.mac }}'. Update host_vars with
    92:           the stanza below.
    93:       when: >-
    94:         (rpi_serial | default('')) != rpi_eeprom_facts.serial8
    95:         or (rpi_board_mac | upper) != rpi_eeprom_facts.mac
    96: 
    97:     - name: Emit inventory stanza for this Pi
    98:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    99:         msg:
   100:           - "# inventory.yaml (under rpis > {{ rpi_board_model }}):"
   101:           - "{{ inventory_hostname }}:"
   102:           - "  rpi_board_mac: \"{{ rpi_eeprom_facts.mac }}\""
   103:           - "  rpi_serial: \"{{ rpi_eeprom_facts.serial8 }}\""
   104:           - "  rpi_boot_mode: {{ rpi_boot_mode }}"
   105:           - "# rb5009 host_vars /ip/dhcp-server/lease (MAC-only, outside 10.10.9.24/29):"
   106:           - "#   address=<10.10.9.x> mac-address={{ rpi_eeprom_facts.mac }} comment={{ inventory_hostname.split('.')[0] }}"
   107:           - "# bootloader: {{ rpi_eeprom_facts.bootloader_version }}"
   108: 
   109:     - name: Record enrollment facts for AAP workflows
   110:       ansible.builtin.set_stats:
   111:         data:
   112:           rpi_enrolled_serials: >-
   113:             {{ {inventory_hostname: {'serial8': rpi_eeprom_facts.serial8,
   114:                                      'mac': rpi_eeprom_facts.mac}} }}

name: playbooks/rpi_netboot/stage_netboot_assets.yml
review_question: Does this playbook have harmful dependency coupling?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Per-Pi netboot staging: netboot server first, then the router.
     3: #   1. rpis group: resolve contract + TFTP prefix + rootfs src per host.
     4: #   2. netboot_server group: rpi_rootfs role per managed Pi (NFS rootfs
     5: #      + full boot-partition TFTP staging), then fetch each Pi's shared
     6: #      boot assets (firmware/kernel/dtb) to the controller cache.
     7: #   3. rpis group (serial): upload the shared <model>/<build_id> set to
     8: #      the router's flash once (size-gated dedup across Pis on the same
     9: #      build) and register this Pi's per-prefix /ip tftp rows pointing
    10: #      into it. Pin files (config.txt/cmdline.txt) are owned by
    11: #      converge_boot_mode.yml, not staged here.
    12: #
    13: # Scope with -e rpi_group=<group> — not --limit. The plays mix rpis
    14: # with netboot_server, and play 2 loops over the rpis group from the
    15: # netboot_server host, so --limit silently empties it.
    16: - name: Resolve per-Pi config and rootfs sources
    17:   hosts: "{{ rpi_group | default('rpis') }}"
    18:   gather_facts: false
    19:   tasks:
    20:     - name: Resolve effective rpi config
    21:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/_resolve_rpi_config.yml
    22: 
    23:     - name: Resolve rpi_rootfs_src per host
    24:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/_resolve_rootfs_src.yml
    25:       when: rpi_netboot_managed
    26: 
    27: - name: Provision per-Pi NFS rootfs + stage and fetch boot assets
    28:   hosts: "{{ rpi_netboot_server_group | default('netboot_server') }}"
    29:   become: true
    30:   gather_facts: false
    31:   vars:
    32:     _managed_pis: >-
    33:       {{ groups[rpi_group | default('rpis')]
    34:          | map('extract', hostvars)
    35:          | selectattr('rpi_netboot_managed', 'defined')
    36:          | selectattr('rpi_netboot_managed')
    37:          | map(attribute='inventory_hostname') | list }}
    38:     # (host, asset) cross-product for the fetch loop. Built with
    39:     # targeted attribute access only: piping full hostvars dicts through
    40:     # subelements() forces EVERY inherited var to render, and fact-less
    41:     # plays then explode on unrelated vars that template ansible_facts
    42:     # (baseline_user_groups' os_family lookup, first hit at the bench).
    43:     _fetch_pairs: >-
    44:       {%- set out = [] -%}
    45:       {%- for h in _managed_pis -%}
    46:       {%-   for a in hostvars[h].rpi_tftp_assets -%}
    47:       {%-     set _ = out.append({'host': h,
    48:                                   'cache_dir': hostvars[h].rpi_tftp_cache_dir,
    49:                                   'asset': a}) -%}
    50:       {%-   endfor -%}
    51:       {%- endfor -%}
    52:       {{ out }}
    53:   tasks:
    54:     - name: Run rpi_rootfs per Pi
    55:       ansible.builtin.include_role:
    56:         name: rpi_rootfs
    57:       vars:
    58:         rpi_rootfs_src: "{{ hostvars[_pi].rpi_rootfs_src }}"
    59:         rpi_rootfs_src_sha256: "{{ hostvars[_pi].rpi_rootfs_src_sha256 | default('') }}"
    60:         rpi_rootfs_host: "{{ _pi }}"
    61:         rpi_rootfs_force_refresh: "{{ rpi_force_refresh | default(false) }}"
    62:       loop: "{{ _managed_pis }}"
    63:       loop_control:
    64:         loop_var: _pi
    65: 
    66:     - name: Ensure controller cache dir exists per host
    67:       ansible.builtin.file:
    68:         path: "{{ hostvars[item].rpi_tftp_cache_dir }}/{{ item }}"
    69:         state: directory
    70:         mode: "0755"
    71:       delegate_to: localhost
    72:       # Force a real local connection: inventory `localhost` defaults to
    73:       # SSH (it is an SSH-able build host), and this devcontainer's sshd
    74:       # has PrivateTmp, so an SSH-delegated mkdir creates a private /tmp
    75:       # the fetch below (controller-side write) cannot see.
    76:       vars:
    77:         ansible_connection: local
    78:       become: false
    79:       loop: "{{ _managed_pis }}"
    80: 
    81:     - name: Fetch each (host, asset) pair from netboot server
    82:       ansible.builtin.fetch:
    83:         src: "{{ rpi_image_cache }}/rpi-tftp/{{ item.host }}/{{ item.asset }}"
    84:         dest: "{{ item.cache_dir }}/{{ item.host }}/{{ item.asset }}"
    85:         flat: true
    86:       loop: "{{ _fetch_pairs }}"
    87:       loop_control:
    88:         label: "{{ item.host }}/{{ item.asset }}"
    89: 
    90: - name: Upload shared TFTP assets to router and register per-Pi rows
    91:   hosts: "{{ rpi_group | default('rpis') }}"
    92:   gather_facts: false
    93:   # One Pi at a time: every host's uploads delegate to the same router,
    94:   # and parallel net_put bursts flake RouterOS's SSH server.
    95:   serial: 1
    96:   vars:
    97:     _shared_dir: "{{ rpi_tftp_flash_dir }}/shared/{{ rpi_board_model }}/{{ rpi_build_id }}"
    98:     # Every build still referenced by a managed Pi of this model — the
    99:     # prune step below must not delete a sibling Pi's active build.
   100:     _active_builds: >-
   101:       {{ groups[rpi_group | default('rpis')]
   102:          | map('extract', hostvars)
   103:          | selectattr('rpi_netboot_managed', 'defined')
   104:          | selectattr('rpi_netboot_managed')
   105:          | selectattr('rpi_board_model', 'equalto', rpi_board_model)
   106:          | map(attribute='rpi_build_id') | unique | list }}
   107:   tasks:
   108:     - name: Stage this Pi's assets on the router
   109:       delegate_to: "{{ rpi_router }}"
   110:       when: rpi_netboot_managed
   111:       block:
   112:         - name: Assert the TFTP prefix is derivable
   113:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: transport/assert_tftp_prefix.yml
   114: 
   115:         - name: Ensure shared dir hierarchy exists on router flash
   116:           community.routeros.command:
   117:             commands:
   118:               - >-
   119:                 :if ([/file find name="{{ item }}" type=directory] = "")
   120:                 do={/file add name="{{ item }}" type=directory}
   121:           register: _shareddir
   122:           retries: 3
   123:           delay: 5
   124:           until: _shareddir is succeeded
   125:           changed_when: false
   126:           loop:
   127:             - "{{ rpi_tftp_flash_dir }}/shared"
   128:             - "{{ rpi_tftp_flash_dir }}/shared/{{ rpi_board_model }}"
   129:             - "{{ _shared_dir }}"
   130: 
   131:         - name: Retarget this Pi's rows onto the current build dir
   132:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: transport/retarget_tftp_row.yml
   133:           vars:
   134:             _retarget_req: "{{ rpi_tftp_prefix }}/{{ item }}"
   135:             _retarget_real: "{{ _shared_dir }}/{{ item }}"
   136:           loop: "{{ rpi_tftp_assets }}"
   137: 
   138:         - name: Upload each shared asset + register this Pi's row
   139:           # Reuses the armbian domain's generic size-gated primitive —
   140:           # it only consumes _upload_* vars. The shared path is keyed by
   141:           # build_id (immutable content), so the size gate is safe and
   142:           # dedups the upload across Pis on the same build.
   143:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: ../armbian/transport/upload_file.yml
   144:           vars:
   145:             _upload_local_src: "{{ rpi_tftp_cache_dir }}/{{ inventory_hostname }}/{{ item }}"
   146:             _upload_remote_path: "{{ _shared_dir }}/{{ item }}"
   147:             _upload_req_filename: "{{ rpi_tftp_prefix }}/{{ item }}"
   148:             _upload_req_filename_is_regex: false
   149:           loop: "{{ rpi_tftp_assets }}"
   150: 
   151:         - name: Prune shared build dirs no longer referenced by any Pi of this model
   152:           community.routeros.command:
   153:             commands:
   154:               - >-
   155:                 /file remove
   156:                 [find where name~"^{{ rpi_tftp_flash_dir }}/shared/{{ rpi_board_model }}/"
   157:                 and !(name~"({{ _active_builds | join('|') }})")]
   158:           register: _prune
   159:           retries: 3
   160:           delay: 5
   161:           until: _prune is succeeded
   162:           # Unconditional remove — RouterOS gives no removed-count back,
   163:           # so report changed rather than hide real mutations from AAP
   164:           # run summaries.
   165:           changed_when: true
   166: 
   167:         - name: Verify /ip tftp rows landed (plumbing check)
   168:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: transport/plumbing_check.yml

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Deploy a release or other branch on a server
     3: #
     4: # This playbook will create a new folder to build the app with Ruby and JS dependencies, and swap
     5: # over for a (relatively) seamless update.
     6: #
     7: # git_version: specify a git ref for the openfoodnetwork codebase (default is master). Eg:
     8: #  -e "git_version=v3.7.0"
     9: #
    10: # github_key: specify a forked branch instead. Eg:
    11: #  -e "github_key=jibees:upgrade-node-version"
    12: #
    13: # This playbook is copied onto staging servers with setup_remote_deployment so they can deploy to
    14: # themselves. It is executed via /home/ofn-deploy/deploy script, which ensures latest version of
    15: # ofn-install is pulled.
    16: 
    17: - name: deploy
    18:   hosts: ofn_servers
    19:   strategy: free
    20:   remote_user: "{{ user }}"
    21:   become: yes
    22:   become_user: "{{ app_user }}"
    23: 
    24:   handlers:
    25:     - import_tasks: ../roles/shared_handlers/handlers/main.yml
    26: 
    27:   tasks:
    28:     - name: Check we're not deploying master to production
    29:       fail:
    30:         msg: |
    31:           WARNING: The current settings would deploy `master` branch to a production server!
    32:           Specify a release when deploying by adding (for example) ` -e "git_version=v3.7.0"`
    33:           to the comand. If you still see this message, check for typos :)
    34:           Latest releases here: https://github.com/openfoodfoundation/openfoodnetwork/releases
    35:       when: rails_env == "production" and git_version == "master"
    36: 
    37:     - block:
    38:       - include_role:
    39:           name: deploy
    40: 
    41:       - meta: flush_handlers # Ensure handlers run successfully before reporting success
    42: 
    43:       - name: Notify Slack of successful deployment
    44:         slack:
    45:           token: "T02G54U79/BF25P9F7A/DJdtYaLLUpRJPiu72d8NqgGg"
    46:           msg: '`{{ git_version }}` deployed to {{ inventory_hostname }}'
    47:           channel: "#devops-notifications"
    48:           username: "ansible executed by {{ lookup('env','USER') }}"
    49:         when: inventory_hostname not in groups['local']
    50: 
    51:       rescue:
    52:         - name: Notify slack of deployment failure
    53:           slack:
    54:             token: "T02G54U79/BF25P9F7A/DJdtYaLLUpRJPiu72d8NqgGg"
    55:             msg: 'Deployment FAILED for {{ inventory_hostname }}'
    56:             channel: "#devops-notifications"
    57:             username: "ansible executed by {{ lookup('env','USER') }}"
    58:           when: inventory_hostname not in groups['local']
    59: 
    60:         - debug:
    61:             msg: Deployment failed
    62:           failed_when: True # Ensure Ansible returns a non-zero error code after rescue

     2: - name: Group hosts based on configuration

    32:   tasks:

name: roles/opentelemetry/tasks/gateway.yml
review_question: Does this playbook have harmful dependency coupling?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Gateway collector — OpenTelemetry-recommended "gateway pattern" implementation.
     3: # Called from setup.yml when `opentelemetry_gateway_enabled: true`, *before*
     4: # the helm task so the gateway collector spec AND its supporting resources
     5: # (htpasswd Secret + Ingress) are included in the chart values.
     6: #
     7: # All resources go through helm via:
     8: #   - `collectors.<gateway_name>` (the OpenTelemetryCollector CR + the
     9: #     operator-spawned Service/Deployment) → driven by
    10: #     `opentelemetry_collectors[<gateway_name>]`
    11: #   - `extraObjects[]` (Secret + Ingress) → driven by
    12: #     `opentelemetry_additional_config.extraObjects`
    13: #
    14: # That way helm owns the full lifecycle: a `helm upgrade` after disabling
    15: # the gateway tears everything down, and credential rotation is reflected
    16: # through a pod-annotation checksum so the operator triggers a rollout.
    17: 
    18: - name: "Compute gateway derived values"
    19:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    20:     _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}"
    21:     _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}-htpasswd"
    22:     _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled: "{{ (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | default('') | length) > 0 }}"
    23: 
    24: - name: "Build the gateway collector spec"
    25:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    26:     opentelemetry_collectors: >-
    27:       {{
    28:         (opentelemetry_collectors | default({}))
    29:         | combine({ opentelemetry_gateway_name: _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec }, recursive=True)
    30:       }}
    31:   vars:
    32:     _volumes: >-
    33:       {{
    34:         [{
    35:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    36:           'secret': {'secretName': _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name}
    37:         }]
    38:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    39:       }}
    40:     _volume_mounts: >-
    41:       {{
    42:         [{
    43:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    44:           'mountPath': '/etc/otel-auth',
    45:           'readOnly': true
    46:         }]
    47:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    48:       }}
    49:     # Credential rotation: the basicauth/server extension caches the
    50:     # htpasswd file at startup, so secret content changes only take effect
    51:     # when the pod restarts. Putting a checksum of the content in
    52:     # podAnnotations makes the operator roll the pod whenever the content
    53:     # differs from the previous apply.
    54:     _pod_annotations: >-
    55:       {{
    56:         {'checksum/htpasswd': (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | hash('sha256'))}
    57:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    58:       }}
    59:     _extensions: >-
    60:       {{
    61:         {'basicauth/server': {'htpasswd': {'file': '/etc/otel-auth/htpasswd'}}}
    62:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    63:       }}
    64:     _service_extensions: >-
    65:       {{
    66:         ['basicauth/server']
    67:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    68:       }}
    69:     # Auto-wire basicauth/server onto the OTLP HTTP receiver. We deep-merge
    70:     # so the user keeps full control of receiver options (compression,
    71:     # max_recv_msg_size, …).
    72:     _otlp_http_auth_overlay:
    73:       otlp:
    74:         protocols:
    75:           http:
    76:             auth:
    77:               authenticator: "basicauth/server"
    78:     _receivers: >-
    79:       {{
    80:         opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    81:         | combine(_otlp_http_auth_overlay, recursive=True)
    82:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled
    83:         else opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    84:       }}
    85:     # If the user did not provide explicit pipelines, route every receiver +
    86:     # processor + exporter into metrics & logs pipelines. Works for the
    87:     # common case of homogeneous OTLP exporters; override when you have
    88:     # signal-specific routing.
    89:     _default_pipelines:
    90:       metrics:
    91:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    92:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    93:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    94:       logs:
    95:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    96:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    97:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    98:     _pipelines: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines if (opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines | length > 0) else _default_pipelines }}"
    99:     _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec:
   100:       enabled: true
   101:       mode: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_mode }}"
   102:       replicas: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_replicas }}"
   103:       # Predictable service name (`<release>-<gateway_name>-collector`),
   104:       # otherwise the chart defaults to `<release>-collector` which
   105:       # collides with any other non-daemon collector. Required for the
   106:       # Ingress backend reference below.
   107:       fullnameOverride: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   108:       resources: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_resources }}"
   109:       volumes: "{{ _volumes }}"
   110:       volumeMounts: "{{ _volume_mounts }}"
   111:       podAnnotations: "{{ _pod_annotations }}"
   112:       config:
   113:         extensions: "{{ _extensions }}"
   114:         receivers: "{{ _receivers }}"
   115:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors }}"
   116:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters }}"
   117:         service:
   118:           extensions: "{{ _service_extensions }}"
   119:           pipelines: "{{ _pipelines }}"
   120: 
   121: - name: "Inject the gateway Secret + Ingress as chart extraObjects"
   122:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   123:     opentelemetry_additional_config: >-
   124:       {{
   125:         (opentelemetry_additional_config | default({}))
   126:         | combine({
   127:             'extraObjects': (
   128:               ((opentelemetry_additional_config | default({})).extraObjects | default([]))
   129:               + _gateway_extra_objects
   130:             )
   131:           })
   132:       }}
   133:   when: _gateway_extra_objects | length > 0
   134:   vars:
   135:     _htpasswd_secret_obj:
   136:       apiVersion: "v1"
   137:       kind: "Secret"
   138:       metadata:
   139:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name }}"
   140:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   141:       type: "Opaque"
   142:       stringData:
   143:         htpasswd: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd }}"
   144:     _ingress_obj:
   145:       apiVersion: "networking.k8s.io/v1"
   146:       kind: "Ingress"
   147:       metadata:
   148:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   149:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   150:         annotations: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_annotations }}"
   151:       spec:
   152:         ingressClassName: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_class_name }}"
   153:         tls: >-
   154:           {{
   155:             [{
   156:               'hosts': [opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname],
   157:               'secretName': opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_secret_name
   158:             }]
   159:             if opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_enabled else []
   160:           }}
   161:         rules:
   162:           - host: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname }}"
   163:             http:
   164:               paths:
   165:                 - path: "/"
   166:                   pathType: "Prefix"
   167:                   backend:
   168:                     service:
   169:                       name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}-collector"
   170:                       port:
   171:                         name: "otlp-http"
   172:     _gateway_extra_objects: >-
   173:       {{
   174:         ([_htpasswd_secret_obj] if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else [])
   175:         + ([_ingress_obj] if opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_enabled else [])
   176:       }}
